$comment: Tailzu's core and the signals people know it by. Read from the brand's own site and repo (tailzu.space: index.html, README.md, favicon.svg, og.png, structured data) and the owner's notes. Every fact here is on the site; nothing is invented. Content comes from this core, never from restating the website.

core.belief: The way you talk is already good enough to send. Your words, your languages and your names belong in the message exactly as you said them; only the mess should go.
core.change: You stop translating your thoughts into thumb-typing: you say it as it comes (half-formed, Hinglish, full of 'um'), and a clean message in your own words lands in whatever app you were in.
core.tension: People think in speech but are made to perform in type. Typing is slow and makes you stiffer or sloppier than you are, and plain dictation writes down every 'um'. Tailzu keeps your voice and drops only the noise: it cleans, it never rewrites.
dramaticTruths: It cleans. It never rewrites: names and amounts stay exactly as you said them.
Two languages stay two: Hinglish is written as Hinglish, not translated.
Your voice leaves, your words stay: audio is deleted once it is written, not stored by default.
It is a keyboard, so it works wherever you can type: WhatsApp, mail, a ChatGPT box, a code editor.
Same words, your tone: one message can be written in eight tones, from Neutral to Noir.

pillars.name: Said → Written
pillars.job: Show the product's whole idea in one pair: the sentence as you said it (hand) and as it lands (type).

pillars.name: Same words, your tone
pillars.job: Play: one rough message in eight tones (Neutral, Casual, Formal, Excited, Shakespeare, Pirate, Movie Trailer, Noir).

pillars.name: Where it lands
pillars.job: The customer's moments: a message to family, a prompt to an AI chat, a change in a code editor, a reply to work.

pillars.name: Kept
pillars.job: Trust and proof: names, amounts and your mix of languages stay; audio is deleted once written; 800 free words a month.

pillars.name: Your language
pillars.job: Hinglish native, 22 Indian languages, native script or English letters: you never have to switch to type.

marks.$comment: Original files copied unchanged from the brand's site repo. Never redraw, simplify or substitute them.

files.from: products/tailzu/logo/humanist-logo.mjs (owner's brief: three keycaps only, Humanist Minimal, more negative space; kept in black)
files.what: The mark: three hand-cut paper keycaps in the original constellation on a Wada Black tile, one key in Yellow Ocher (the brand's amber, 'alive, right now'), no connecting lines. Vector, 1000 x 1000.

The mark: three cream keycaps joined by lines (a pale line, an amber dashed link, a copper tail ending in a dot) on the app's near-black tile. Vector, 1000 × 1000. Retired: replaced by the Humanist Minimal mark (owner approved, 2026-10-09). Kept for reference.
App icon, 512 × 512 (the logo in the site's structured data).

marks.usage: The mark is the black tile (tailzu-mark-dark.svg), approved by the owner on 2026-10-09: always the black version, on every ground; never recoloured, redrawn or set without its tile. The blue and light tiles and the tile-less marks in assets/logos/humanist/ were proposals and are not used. The brand has no wordmark font of its own; where a name is needed it is set in the pairing's sans beside the mark.
marks.$engine: kind (icon | wordmark | lockup) and on (dark | light | any) tell the design engine which original file to place; only files with a kind are used.

type.role: Spaced capital labels (SAID, WRITTEN, TYPED) and the footer.
Speech: 'Speech is a person, and a person writes by hand' (README, The river).

signals.imagery: No photography. Dark, calm grounds; speech drawn as handwriting arriving from the edges and swallowed by one set word; UI drawn plainly (a message field, a chat box, a code editor, a keyboard). Light comes from one place, never from a second colour.
signatureElements: Hand in, type out: the said line in handwriting, the written line in a calm serif (og.png, the river).
SAID / WRITTEN labels in spaced mono capitals.
The amber full stop that lands last on the written line.
Proof-reading marks: on the site's hero 'key' is struck through and 'keyless' is written above it, the way an editor marks a proof.
A kept word is underlined, not coloured: 'a fact that survived is a record, not a thing still in play' (README).
The three keycaps of the mark, joined like a constellation.
